scope: Isolated local HTTP and Headless Chrome, 1366 x 900. Frozen current tournament: 512 games, 423 finished, 15 courts. All writes and services simulated. No live BTS or BTP changes; no player names or captured contents in this report.

method.visible_ms: Navigation start to bts-board-visible: visible sections built and fitted; fonts loaded, no pending layout jobs over consecutive animation frames. Distant rows may still be pending. Baseline: second settled frame of its eager build.
method.navigation_to_ready_ms: Navigation start to visible main view and three consecutive animation frames with no ctournament or cleitstand work, including all startup sections. Remains the old full-load measurement.
method.cold: Fresh Chrome profile, empty HTTP cache and session storage; a new isolated asset server instance for each profile.
method.reload: Three actual Page.reload(ignoreCache:false) calls in each profile. Every tournament response fetched without cache.
method.order: before-1, after-1, after-2, before-2, after-3, before-3, before-4, after-4; four cold calls and twelve reloads per variant; no CPU profiler or concurrent browser tests.
method.limits: Local timing samples are not production latency guarantees. CPU scheduling and render-frame alignment vary. First visible load is distinct from complete offscreen preparation; a cold complete build still exceeds one second.

implementation: Build court rows, controls and enough upcoming rows to fill the viewport first. Verify actual section coverage for hidden halls, date groups and browser zoom.
Build all remaining upcoming rows and the existing 50 selected results in tasks directly after the visible paint; no scroll trigger, idle callback or persistent content-visibility skip.
Keep model data and pending row identities. Materialize from the current model, preserving already visible rows, controls, focus and cache behavior.
Share an initial-render job with affected incoming update receipts; court points remain independent. Cancel work and release callbacks when leaving the board.
Reattach history paging controls after rebuilding its initial table; protect browser-only font/metrics setup so pure Node helpers remain testable.

operating_comparison.method: Two before and two after browser sessions, ten finish/edit/point/reopen cycles each after startup has fully settled. Includes bursts of sixteen concurrent upcoming edits. Independent render frames confirm each unrelated point.
operating_comparison.interpretation: Repeated comparison has essentially identical mean point and finish latency. Reopening varies by about one render frame. Earlier series showed higher candidate CPU and frame wait times, so they were repeated instead of selecting a single favorable run. Counts/structure are identical; these small samples do not prove a universal latency bound.
